entry.title: They live by a shrine to a saint. Why are their homes being demolished?
entry.summary: The neighborhood is a pilgrimage site, with a shrine to the Sufi saint known as Bari Imam. In the past year, hundreds of homes of the working poor were razed. Residents fear more will be demolished.

entry.title: A NY hospital tried to close its birthing center. This city united to fight back
entry.summary: Democrats and Republicans in Troy, New York, took on a national Catholic health system and kept the county's last birthing center open.

entry.title: Whatever happened to the U.S. famine alert system that Trump shut down, then reopened
entry.summary: The highly regarded FEWS NET network stopped posting data on Afghanistan, Somalia and Yemen -- then says it will start posting again in September. What's the reason for this back-and-forth?

entry.title: NPR's 2-year search for the truth about deaths from heat
entry.summary: An investigation from NPR and Boston University finds that heat kills thousands of Americans every year. But official numbers radically undercount heat deaths.

entry.title: Why too many women are prescribed antibiotics for UTIs they don't have
entry.summary: A recent study found that many women treated for recurrent UTIs didn't have UTIs at all. Instead, their symptoms were caused by hormonally driven inflammation and pelvic floor dysfunction.

entry.title: Dry eyes are common among women. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it
entry.summary: Dry eyes are a very common chronic eye condition among women in perimenopause and beyond. Here's why you shouldn't ignore it.

entry.title: Medicare's pilot GLP-1 discount program has a catch. Some sick patients don't qualify
entry.summary: Medicare launched a pilot program that could streamline the process to get GLP-1s, with some seniors paying just $50 a month. But many people with the most serious illnesses won't get that discount.

entry.title: The bridges of Rwanda open up new worlds
entry.summary: A charity built 96 bridges to connect communities separated by rivers and gorges. A new study looks at the life-changing impact of a concrete-and-steel pedestrian crossing.

entry.title: Pennsylvania measles deaths ignite clash over RFK Jr.'s vaccination claims
entry.summary: Two deaths associated with the measles outbreak in Pennsylvania prompted messaging from the health secretary that both encouraged and undermined vaccinations.

entry.title: Lights out, Instagram off? The changes to Meta for teens could be a big deal
entry.summary: Researchers and advocates are applauding the changes that Meta agreed to make for minors on Instagram and Facebook. Cutting kids off at night and during the school day are two big changes.
